title: Quantum Oscillation Signatures of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Monopole Charge in Nodal-Ring Semimetals
authors: Aravind Karthigeyan, Yoonseok Hwang, Bohm-Jung Yang, Junyeong Ahn
abstract: Topological semimetals host band nodes characterized by quantized invariants that can appear in bulk responses, yet some invariants remain hidden from standard probes. In particular, band nodes can carry secondary topological charges whose transport signatures are still largely unexplored. Here we study three-dimensional nodal-line semimetals in which nodal rings carry both the Berry phase $w_1π$ and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopole charge $w_2$. We show that magnetic quantum oscillations, usually treated as a probe of $w_1$, can directly diagnose $w_2$, with the relevant signal selected by the magnetic-field direction. For a field along the ring axis, the inner and outer extremal orbits of the toroidal Fermi surface both encircle the $w_2$-enforced thread and exhibit a topological phase shift $νw_2π$ in the $ν$th harmonic, which is accessible through standard phase-resolved quantum-oscillation analysis. By contrast, for a field applied perpendicular to the ring axis, the relevant extremal orbit exhibits the usual $π$ phase shift associated with the Berry phase $w_1π$, independent of $w_2$. For weak doping, three-dimensional ABC-stacked graphdiyne is predicted to exhibit the proposed oscillations in a field range accessible with present-day high-field facilities.
summary: This work proposes using magnetic quantum oscillations to detect a secondary topological invariant—the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopole charge ($w_2$)—in nodal-line semimetals. The key diagnostic is observing a specific $\pi$ phase shift in the oscillation signal when the field is applied parallel to the ring axis. Graphdiyne is identified as the most promising material candidate for experimental verification.
main_problem: The primary goal is to find a measurable bulk transport signature that can distinguish nodal-line semimetals possessing a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopole charge ($w_2=1$) from those without ($w_2=0$).
main_result: Magnetic quantum oscillations, specifically the phase shift in the oscillatory conductivity when the magnetic field is parallel to the ring axis, can directly diagnose the presence of the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopole charge by predicting a topological phase shift of $\pi$.
method: The analysis uses semiclassical theory applied to nodal-line semimetals, calculating quantum oscillations via the Lifshitz–Kosevich formula and extracting topological information from the phase offset ($\gamma$) in the oscillatory conductivity.
model_or_system: The study focuses on three-dimensional nodal-line semimetals containing 'nodal rings' that can host both a Berry phase ($w_1\pi$) and a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ monopole charge ($w_2$). ABC-stacked graphdiyne is presented as the most promising candidate material.
key_observables: Magnetic quantum oscillation phase offset ($\gamma$), which is sensitive to the topological invariant $w_2$.
important_parameters: The magnetic field direction relative to the ring axis, and the ratio of SOC scales to characteristic energy scales (e.g., $\Delta\text{SOC}/E_F$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes closed nodal rings with toroidal Fermi surfaces; for material screening, it requires weak Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) relative to other energy scales.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the cyclotron orbit geometry showing how $\mathbf{B} \parallel \hat{z}$ leads to a $\pi$ phase shift for $w_2=1$, while $\mathbf{B} \parallel \hat{x}$ shows standard Berry phase behavior. Other figures show FFTs of conductivity and Landau fans.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving continuum Landau spectra, establishing the diagnostic role of the phase shift ($\Phi_{\phi}$) for $\mathbf{B} \parallel \hat{z}$, and then applies this test to screen various material platforms (graphdiyne, TMDs, Si/Ge) based on their predicted SOC scales.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter topology, the reliance on precise semiclassical quantization rules and topological invariants makes it relevant for understanding boundary conditions in quantum systems, which has parallels with open quantum system dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Cyclotron-orbit geometry for a toroidal Fermi surface around a Z2 monopole nodal ring. (a) For B ∥ˆz, the inner and outer extremal orbits both encircle the thread and carry the toroidal Berry phase Φϕ = π, giving the two Onsager frequencies F±. (b) For B ∥ˆx, linking orbits at kx = 0 carry Φθ = π, while nonlinking maximal orbits at kx = ±k∗ x have Φ = 0 and give F ∗.

FIG. 2. Energy-momentum dispersion of the Z2 monopole nodal ring in Eq. (1). (a) At kz = 0 and ky = 0, the conduc- tion and valence branches meet at |kx| = m0, corresponding to the nodal ring at kρ = m0. (b) Along kx = ky = 0, the oc- cupied (and unoccupied) bands are twofold degenerate for all kz, forming the linked “thread” in the occupied/unoccupied subspace.

(a) Total yz-section area Ayz(kx) (units of m2 0); the kx = 0 section consists of two degenerate linking loops of area Ayz(0)/2 each, giving F0, while kx = ±k∗ x gives nonlinking maximal loops and F ∗.
